name: Supreme Power Equipment Ltd
tagline: Debt-free small-cap transformer manufacturer (power/generator/windmill transformers, Chennai) riding the grid-capex and renewables tailwind, mid-way through a 3.6x capacity expansion (2,500 -> 9,000 MVA, Kanpur facility ~95% complete) with an order book at ~2x conservative FY27 revenue guidance - real execution but PAT growth is lagging revenue growth on new-plant overhead absorption, and moat vs the established transformer-maker peer set is still unclear beyond a 220kV positioning niche.
business_overview: Incorporated 1994, Supreme Power Equipment manufactures, upgrades and renovates power transformers, generator transformers and windmill/wind-turbine transformers, serving India's power-sector capex and renewables buildout, based in Chennai with a new manufacturing facility in Kanpur. Seeded via untrusted X triage (@rdkriplani, bullish, medium conviction, 2026-09-13).
fundamentals_table: ROCE ~21.5% (screener FY26); ROE ~19.4% latest yr / ~22.6% 3-yr avg (sources show a range up to ROCE 29.4% depending on window)
FY26 revenue from ops Rs 190.08 Cr vs Rs 144.80 Cr FY25 (+31.3%); 3-yr sales CAGR ~36%, 5-yr ~40%

FY26 PAT Rs 20.44 Cr vs Rs 18.60 Cr FY25 (+9.9%) - profit growth materially lagging revenue growth (3-yr profit CAGR ~24% vs sales ~36%), driven by new-plant (Kanpur) overhead absorption during ramp-up
D/E ~0.08-0.085x (borrowings ~Rs 46-72 Cr vs equity ~Rs 118 Cr) - near debt-free, more cash than total debt
New Kanpur facility (~6 acres, ~Rs 95-100 Cr capex, ~95% complete) lifts capacity from 2,500 MVA to 9,000 MVA (3.6x); currently running at 20-28% utilisation, guided to reach 30-50% by Q4 FY27

Rs 590 Cr as of mid-Aug 2026 (30.1% government / 69.9% private; power transformers 76.9% of orders) vs a conservative FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 250-300 Cr - ~2x revenue cover with 7-17 month execution timelines
fundamentals_narrative: Genuinely strong top-line growth (31% FY26 revenue growth, 36% 3-yr CAGR) and a clean balance sheet (near-zero net debt, ROCE/ROE both in the 20%+ range), riding real power-sector and renewables transformer demand, now backed by a large, funded capacity expansion (2,500 -> 9,000 MVA at the new Kanpur facility, ~95% complete) rather than just an order-book story. However, profit growth has lagged revenue growth for two straight periods (FY26 PAT +9.9% vs revenue +31.3%; Q1 FY27 PAT +10.0% vs revenue +37.3%) - management attributes this explicitly to Kanpur's new-plant overhead being absorbed ahead of utilisation catching up (currently only 20-28% utilised), which is a normal capex-ramp pattern rather than a structural margin problem, but it means near-term earnings will lag the revenue growth headline. FY26 operating cash flow (~Rs 28 Cr) fell short of capex (~Rs 40 Cr), producing negative free cash flow for the year - again consistent with a genuine capex-ramp phase, not an operating red flag, but worth tracking given management has flagged potential equity dilution by FY28 for further expansion. The transformer-manufacturing space in India remains crowded with several small/mid-cap listed peers (Shilchar Technologies, TARIL, Voltamp Transformers, Raychem RPG, Danish Power), most of which sit at 132kV and below; Supreme's stated positioning in the 220kV segment (fewer competitors, higher realisation per MVA) is a potential differentiator worth watching but is not yet proven at scale, and the company has secured no export orders to date (management expects 'a few more years' for meaningful export traction). Order book quality looks reasonable: 80-85% is covered by price-variation clauses (protecting margins from input-cost swings), and the government/private split (30%/70%) is balanced rather than concentrated. P/E of ~25-26x is not obviously cheap for the growth on offer, but is not stretched either given the capacity-ramp optionality.

verdict_headline: Fast-growing, debt-free small-cap transformer maker with a real, funded 3.6x capacity expansion and an order book covering ~2x conservative guidance - a genuine capex-ramp inflection story, but profit growth is lagging revenue growth on new-plant overhead absorption and moat vs the established peer set remains unproven beyond a 220kV niche claim. Conviction stays Medium; thesis_fit stays 'neither' on a four_box score of 2.5.
verdict_reasoning: four_box re-derived at 2.5 (tailwind yes - real power-capex/renewables demand plus a specific 220kV under-served niche; tam weak - domestic-only, no exports yet, and land-constrained beyond the current build; moat weak - crowded peer set, 220kV positioning is a plausible but unproven differentiator; valuation weak - P/E ~25-26x is not a bargain for a business whose PAT growth is currently lagging revenue growth). 2.5 sits in the 2.0-2.5 band, which mandates thesis_fit 'neither' with no clean written exception (valuation is not 'yes', and growth, while genuinely strong on revenue, is not yet un-ignorable on the bottom line given the overhead-absorption drag) - no analyst_override needed since the score itself now dictates 'neither'.

Conviction held at Medium rather than upgraded: the capacity-expansion execution (95% complete, on the guided utilisation ramp) and disciplined order-book/guidance behaviour are real positives that keep this above Low-Medium, but the lack of independent ValuePickr-thread corroboration this pass, the unresolved profit-vs-revenue growth gap, and the flagged FY28 equity-dilution risk keep it from moving to Medium-High.
No red flag found this pass; near-zero debt and no pledge/governance issues surfaced.

The Kanpur utilisation ramp (20-28% now, guided 30-50% by Q4 FY27) and the FY27 revenue delivery against the Rs 590 Cr order book are the key things to track before conviction could move meaningfully in either direction.

four_box.note: Real power-capex/renewables tailwind and a specific, funded capacity-doubling-plus execution story support tailwind=yes; TAM capped by domestic-only exposure (no exports yet, land-constrained beyond current build) and moat unproven beyond an unverified 220kV niche claim in a crowded peer field; valuation (~25-26x) is not cheap for a business whose PAT growth currently lags revenue growth on overhead absorption - kept at 'neither'.
